claim: The study cohort consisted of 106 trans women who underwent standardized GAHT comprising estrogens and cyproterone acetate.
source: Therefore, this study aimed to characterize, through histological and transcriptomic analysis, the spermatogonial stem cell niche of 106 trans women who underwent standardized GAHT, comprising estrogens and cyproterone acetate.
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states the sample size and treatment regimen in the abstract.

claim: A partial dedifferentiation of Sertoli cells was observed in trans women, marked by the co-expression of androgen receptor and anti-Müllerian hormone.
source: A partial dedifferentiation of Sertoli cells was observed, marked by the co-expression of androgen receptor and anti-Müllerian hormone which mirrors the situation in peripubertal boys.
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by immunohistochemistry data presented in the manuscript.

claim: The Sertoli cell phenotype in trans women mirrors the situation in peripubertal boys.
source: A partial dedifferentiation of Sertoli cells was observed, marked by the co-expression of androgen receptor and anti-Müllerian hormone which mirrors the situation in peripubertal boys.
evidence: This comparison is based on immunohistochemical analysis comparing trans women tissue to control tissues.

claim: Leydig cells in trans women exhibited a distribution analogous to peripubertal tissue.
source: The Leydig cells also exhibited a distribution analogous to peripubertal tissue, accompanied by a reduced insulin-like factor 3 expression.
evidence: This finding is based on immunohistochemical analysis of Leydig cell markers.

claim: Leydig cells in trans women showed reduced insulin-like factor 3 expression.
source: The Leydig cells also exhibited a distribution analogous to peripubertal tissue, accompanied by a reduced insulin-like factor 3 expression.
evidence: This is supported by immunofluorescence staining data for INSL3.

claim: Most peritubular myoid cells in trans women expressed alpha-smooth muscle actin 2, but the expression pattern was disturbed.
source: Although most peritubular myoid cells expressed alpha-smooth muscle actin 2, the expression pattern was disturbed.
evidence: This observation is based on ACTA2 immunohistochemistry data.

claim: Fibrosis was particularly evident in the tubular wall of trans women.
source: Besides this, fibrosis was particularly evident in the tubular wall and the lumen was collapsing in most participants.
evidence: This is based on histological examination and hyalinization scoring.

claim: The lumen was collapsing in most trans women participants.
source: Besides this, fibrosis was particularly evident in the tubular wall and the lumen was collapsing in most participants.
evidence: This is based on histological assessment of lumen status.

claim: A spermatogenic arrest was observed in all trans women participants.
source: A spermatogenic arrest was also observed in all participants.
evidence: This is based on immunohistochemical analysis of germ cell differentiation markers.

claim: The transcriptomic profile of transgender tissue confirmed a loss of mature characteristics - a partial rejuvenation - of the spermatogonial stem cell niche.
source: The transcriptomic profile of transgender tissue confirmed a loss of mature characteristics - a partial rejuvenation - of the spermatogonial stem cell niche and, in addition, detected inflammation processes occurring in the samples.
evidence: This is based on RNA sequencing and differential gene expression analysis.

claim: Inflammation processes were detected in transgender testicular tissue samples.
source: The transcriptomic profile of transgender tissue confirmed a loss of mature characteristics - a partial rejuvenation - of the spermatogonial stem cell niche and, in addition, detected inflammation processes occurring in the samples.
evidence: This is based on gene expression analysis and GO term enrichment.

claim: GAHT changes the spermatogonial stem cell niche by partially rejuvenating the somatic cells.
source: The present study shows that GAHT changes the spermatogonial stem cell niche by partially rejuvenating the somatic cells and inducing fibrotic processes.
evidence: This conclusion is based on the combined histological and transcriptomic findings.

claim: GAHT induces fibrotic processes in the testicular tissue.
source: The present study shows that GAHT changes the spermatogonial stem cell niche by partially rejuvenating the somatic cells and inducing fibrotic processes.
evidence: This is based on histological observations and gene expression analysis.

claim: At the time of orchidectomy, participants were 31.0 years of age (median, range 18.1–70.1).
source: At the time of orchidectomy, participants were 31.0 years of age (18.1–70.1) and had been administered GAHT for 1.8 years (0.4–7.0).
evidence: This demographic information is directly stated in the Results section.

claim: Participants had been administered GAHT for 1.8 years (median, range 0.4–7.0).
source: At the time of orchidectomy, participants were 31.0 years of age (18.1–70.1) and had been administered GAHT for 1.8 years (0.4–7.0).
evidence: This treatment duration information is directly stated in the Results section.

claim: All participants had reached adulthood at the time of SRS (Tanner stage G5).
source: All participants had reached adulthood at the time of SRS (Tanner stage G5).

claim: Most participants were treated with oral estrogen (72.6%) rather than transdermal estrogen (27.4%).
source: Most were treated with oral estrogen (72.6%) rather than transdermal estrogen (27.4%), and all participants received the anti-androgen cyproterone acetate (CPA).
evidence: This treatment distribution is directly stated in the Results section.

claim: All participants received the anti-androgen cyproterone acetate (CPA).
source: Most were treated with oral estrogen (72.6%) rather than transdermal estrogen (27.4%), and all participants received the anti-androgen cyproterone acetate (CPA).

claim: None of the participants had received prior treatment with puberty blockers.

claim: Gonadotropins were generally sufficiently suppressed with serum LH levels of 0.10 U/L (median, range 0.09–9.6).
source: In this cohort, generally, the gonadotropins were sufficiently suppressed with serum luteinizing hormone (LH) levels of 0.10 U/L (0.09–9.6) and serum follicle-stimulating hormone (FSH) levels of 0.19 U/L (0.09–12.0).
evidence: This hormone level data is directly stated in the Results section.

evidence: This hormone level data is directly stated in the Results section.

claim: The Endocrine Society and WPATH SOC 8 guidelines advise trans women to maintain serum testosterone levels below 50 ng/dL.
source: Both the Endocrine Society and the WPATH SOC 8 guidelines advise trans women to maintain serum testosterone (T) levels below 50 ng/dL (Hembree et al., 2017; Coleman et al., 2022).
evidence: This guideline recommendation is cited from published clinical guidelines.

claim: The testosterone threshold of 50 ng/dL corresponds to the cisgender premenopausal female as well as the prepubertal male range.
source: This threshold corresponds to the cisgender premenopausal female as well as the prepubertal male range (Kulle et al., 2010) and is met by 90.4% (94/104) of the included participants: 16.84 ng/dL (0.1–45.9).
evidence: This comparison is supported by a citation to published reference ranges.

claim: 90.4% (94/104) of the included participants met the testosterone threshold below 50 ng/dL.
source: This threshold corresponds to the cisgender premenopausal female as well as the prepubertal male range (Kulle et al., 2010) and is met by 90.4% (94/104) of the included participants: 16.84 ng/dL (0.1–45.9).
evidence: This percentage is calculated from the hormone level data in the cohort.

claim: 9.6% of participants (10 individuals) exhibited testosterone levels above 50 ng/dL with a median of 127.4 ng/dL (range 50.8–499.1).
source: The remaining 10 participants (9.6%) exhibited higher T levels: 127.4 ng/dL (50.8–499.1).
evidence: This is calculated from the hormone level data in the cohort.

claim: Three participants (2.9%) showed testosterone levels within the adult male range (>218 ng/dL).
source: Notably, three of these individuals (2.9%) even showed T levels within the adult male range (>218 ng/dL) (Travison et al., 2017).
evidence: This is based on hormone level data compared to cited reference ranges.

claim: The Endocrine Society and WPATH SOC 8 guidelines recommend serum estradiol levels of 100–200 ng/L for trans women.
source: In terms of serum estradiol (E2) levels, the threshold recommended by the Endocrine Society and WPATH SOC 8 guidelines (Hembree et al., 2017; Coleman et al., 2022) is set at 100–200 ng/L and corresponds to the cisgender premenopausal female range (Kushnir et al., 2008).
evidence: This guideline recommendation is cited from published clinical guidelines.

claim: The recommended estradiol threshold of 100–200 ng/L corresponds to the cisgender premenopausal female range.
source: In terms of serum estradiol (E2) levels, the threshold recommended by the Endocrine Society and WPATH SOC 8 guidelines (Hembree et al., 2017; Coleman et al., 2022) is set at 100–200 ng/L and corresponds to the cisgender premenopausal female range (Kushnir et al., 2008).
evidence: This comparison is supported by a citation to published reference ranges.

claim: 74.3% (78/105) of the participants showed estradiol levels below the recommended threshold with a median of 56.8 ng/L (range 14.1–94.7).
source: Remarkably, 74.3% (78/105) of the participants showed E2 levels below this recommendation: 56.8 ng/L (14.1–94.7).

claim: Six participants (5.7%) exceeded the recommended estradiol threshold with a median of 410.5 ng/L (range 250.0–776.0).
source: Besides this, six participants (5.7%) exceeded this threshold: 410.5 ng/L (250.0–776.0).

claim: 21 participants (20.0%) displayed target estradiol levels with a median of 128.0 ng/L (range 102.0–188.0).
source: The remaining 21 participants (20.0%) displayed target E2 levels: 128.0 ng/L (102.0–188.0).

claim: 56% (38/68) of the participants exhibited serum AMH levels within the normal adult range with a median of 5.2 μg/L (range 1.4–11.6).

evidence: This percentage is calculated from the hormone level data in the cohort.

claim: 27 trans women (40%) surpassed the upper reference limit of 11.6 μg/L for AMH and fell within the male peripubertal range with a median of 25.3 μg/L (range 11.8–143).
source: Noteworthy, 27 trans women (40%) surpassed the upper reference limit of 11.6 μg/L and fell within the male peripubertal range: 25.3 μg/L (11.8–143).

claim: Only 23% (16/69) of the trans women showed normal inhibin B levels with a median of 140.7 pg/mL (range 95.9–193.6).

claim: ACTA2 expression is absent in the PTMCs of prepubertal boys.

claim: During puberty, ACTA2 appears in certain seminiferous tubules, resulting in an 'interrupted' pattern.

evidence: This is based on linear regression analysis of the data.

claim: Participants with FSH<0.3 appear to show fewer INSL3+ cells than participants with FSH>0.3 and LH>0.1.
source: The participants with FSH<0.3 appear to show fewer INSL3+ cells than participants with FSH>0.3 and LH>0.1, estimated to differ –19.460.
evidence: This is based on linear regression analysis of the data.

claim: The first component of PCA explaining approximately 90% of the variation differentiated samples according to progression of spermatogenesis and tissue maturity.
source: The first component explaining approximately 90% of the variation (x-axis) differentiated samples according to progression of spermatogenesis and tissue maturity (Figure 5A), locating the transgender transcriptomes next to the prepubertal ones.
evidence: This is based on principal component analysis of RNA sequencing data, with results shown in Figure 5A.

claim: PCA located the transgender transcriptomes next to the prepubertal ones.
source: The first component explaining approximately 90% of the variation (x-axis) differentiated samples according to progression of spermatogenesis and tissue maturity (Figure 5A), locating the transgender transcriptomes next to the prepubertal ones.
evidence: This is based on principal component analysis of RNA sequencing data, with results shown in Figure 5A.

claim: 11,661 differentially expressed genes were detected when comparing the four different types of tissue.
source: When comparing the four different types of tissue, 11,661 differentially expressed genes (DEGs) were found (Figure 5B).
evidence: This is based on differential gene expression analysis, with results shown in Figure 5B.

claim: Most DEGs were found between prepubertal and adult control (9944 DEGs).
source: Most DEGs were found between prepubertal and adult control (9944 DEGs), and adult control and transgender (8563 DEGs).
evidence: This is based on differential gene expression analysis comparing tissue types.

claim: 8563 DEGs were found between adult control and transgender tissue.
source: Most DEGs were found between prepubertal and adult control (9944 DEGs), and adult control and transgender (8563 DEGs).
evidence: This is based on differential gene expression analysis comparing tissue types.

claim: The least DEGs were found between prepubertal and transgender tissue (1676 DEGs), highlighting the similitude between these two tissues at a transcriptomic level.
source: On the other hand, the least DEGs were found between prepubertal and transgender tissue (1676 DEGs), highlighting the similitude between these two tissues also at a transcriptomic level.
evidence: This is based on differential gene expression analysis comparing tissue types.

claim: Pattern P1 is characterized by biological processes related to tissue morphogenesis and development.
source: Pattern P1 is characterized by biological processes related to tissue morphogenesis and development.
evidence: This is based on GO term enrichment analysis of gene expression patterns.

claim: Prepubertal tissue shows the highest gene expression for pattern P1.
source: As expected, prepubertal tissue shows the highest gene expression for this pattern, as the tissue is in development.
evidence: This is based on gene expression heatmap analysis.

claim: Transgender tissue shows a gene expression intensity for P1 similar to that in peripubertal tissue and between adult and prepubertal tissue.
source: Interestingly, transgender tissue shows a gene expression intensity similar to that in peripubertal tissue (particularly donor Peripubertal 1) and between adult and prepubertal tissue.
evidence: This is based on gene expression heatmap analysis.

claim: Pattern P2 is mainly characterized by cellular components that were significantly enriched in the GO terms analysis.
source: For pattern P2, mainly cellular components were significantly enriched in the GO terms analysis, which means that this pattern describes the location where activities and actions of these gene products are executed.
evidence: This is based on GO term enrichment analysis of gene expression patterns.

claim: Pattern P2 can be related to a more stable tissue environment, where most activities happen outside the cells providing structural support, and biochemical or biomechanical cues.
source: Contrary to pattern P1, P2 can be related to a more stable tissue environment, where most activities happen outside the cells providing structural support, and biochemical or biomechanical cues.
evidence: This is an interpretation based on GO term enrichment analysis.

claim: For pattern P2, adult control tissue shows the highest expression.
source: Consequently, for P2, adult control tissue shows the highest expression, and, again, transgender tissue has a similar expression to donor Peripubertal 1.
evidence: This is based on gene expression heatmap analysis.

claim: Pattern P3 represents meiosis and sperm production.
source: Pattern P3 represents meiosis and sperm production.
evidence: This is based on GO term enrichment analysis of gene expression patterns.

claim: Transgender tissue showed a low expression of genes in pattern P3 similar to prepubertal tissue.
source: As expected, since spermatogenesis is repressed in trans women, transgender tissue showed a low expression of genes in this pattern similar to prepubertal tissue.
evidence: This is based on gene expression heatmap analysis.

claim: Pattern P4 is associated with cell components (chromosome and spindle) important in both mitotic and meiotic processes.
source: P4 is associated with cell components (chromosome and spindle) important in both mitotic and meiotic processes.
evidence: This is based on GO term enrichment analysis of gene expression patterns.

claim: Less gene expression for P4 was observed in transgender tissue since it is structurally adult (no mitosis) but does not host spermatogenesis (no meiosis).
source: Thus, as expected, less gene expression for P4 was observed in transgender tissue since it is structurally adult (no mitosis) but does not host spermatogenesis (no meiosis).
evidence: This is based on gene expression heatmap analysis and biological interpretation.

claim: Pattern P5 is a gene expression pattern specific to transgender tissue.
source: P5 is a gene expression pattern specific to transgender tissue.
evidence: This is based on gene expression heatmap analysis showing unique expression in trans women.

claim: Pattern P5 includes several biological processes pointing to active inflammation and fibrosis.
source: This pattern includes several biological processes pointing to active inflammation and fibrosis described by the GO terms 'cell population proliferation' (119 genes, adjusted p-value<5.90e-15), which is not necessarily related to the mitotic cell cycle, but rather an increase in the number of cells in a certain space over a period (due to cell infiltration), 'cell activation' (96, 1.69e-13) or 'leukocyte activation' (83, 5.19e-11), 'cell migration' (95, 1.59e-11), 'cell death' (107, 1.38e-07), 'regulation of cell differentiation' (83, 5.46e-07) if associated with macrophages, e.g., 'response to stimulus' (348, 2.39e-16), 'cellular response to cytokine stimulus' (72, 3.05e-10), 'response to growth factor' (49, 7.02e-07), 'regulation of multicellular organismal process' (167, 4.21e-22), and 'extracellular matrix organization' (44, 8.84e-13).
evidence: This is based on GO term enrichment analysis of gene expression pattern P5.

claim: Pattern P5 includes tumorigenesis-related processes suggested by the GO terms 'angiogenesis' and 'MAPK cascade'.
source: In addition, commonly associated with inflammation and fibrosis, tumorigenesis-related processes suggested by the GO terms 'angiogenesis' (56, 4.43e-14) and 'MAPK cascade' (53, 9.85e-06) are also part of P5.
evidence: This is based on GO term enrichment analysis of gene expression pattern P5.

claim: The GO term 'response to estrogen' is part of pattern P5, suggesting the particularity of this expression pattern to transgender tissue.
source: Also noteworthy, is the GO term 'response to estrogen' (8, 1.55e-2) in P5, suggesting the particularity of this expression pattern to transgender tissue.
evidence: This is based on GO term enrichment analysis of gene expression pattern P5.

claim: Trans woman 6 shows the highest expression for pattern P5, which is also the most fibrotic tissue out of the six transgender tissues used for gene expression analysis.
source: Highlighting these findings, trans woman 6 shows the highest expression for this pattern, which is also the most fibrotic tissue out of the six transgender tissues used for the gene expression analysis (pictures not shown).
evidence: This is based on gene expression heatmap analysis correlated with histological observations.

claim: GAHT can significantly change the adult testis transcriptome to a less mature one.
source: Taken together, these findings suggest that GAHT can significantly change the adult testis transcriptome to a less mature one, as well as initiate other biological processes that are not normally activated in the testis transcriptome.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the transcriptomic analysis comparing trans women to controls.

claim: GAHT initiates biological processes that are not normally activated in the testis transcriptome.
source: Taken together, these findings suggest that GAHT can significantly change the adult testis transcriptome to a less mature one, as well as initiate other biological processes that are not normally activated in the testis transcriptome.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the transcriptomic analysis, particularly pattern P5.

claim: Previous studies on the impact of GAHT on spermatogenesis in trans women yielded contrasting outcomes, ranging from maturation arrest to full spermatogenesis.
source: Previous studies mainly focused on the impact of GAHT on spermatogenesis, yielding contrasting outcomes, ranging from maturation arrest (Lu and Steinberger, 1978; Sapino et al., 1987; Schulze, 1988; Payer et al., 2009; Leavy et al., 2017; Jindarak et al., 2018; Matoso et al., 2018; Schneider et al., 2019; Vereecke et al., 2020; de Nie et al., 2022a) to full spermatogenesis (Jiang et al., 2019; Alford et al., 2020).
evidence: This is a summary of findings from multiple cited studies.

claim: Varying degrees of tubular hyalinization were found after GAHT in previous studies.
source: Besides this, varying degrees of tubular hyalinization were found after GAHT (Sapino et al., 1987; Schulze, 1988; Venizelos and Paradinas, 1988; Jindarak et al., 2018; Sinha et al., 2021; de Nie et al., 2022b).
evidence: This is a summary of findings from multiple cited studies.

claim: Some studies suggested dedifferentiation of Sertoli cells after GAHT.
source: Some studies also suggested dedifferentiation of Sertoli cells (Schulze, 1988) and/or dedifferentiation or loss of Leydig cells (Rodriguez-Rigau et al., 1977; Sapino et al., 1987; Schulze, 1988; Venizelos and Paradinas, 1988; Kisman et al., 1990; Matoso et al., 2018; Cornejo et al., 2022).
evidence: This is a summary of findings from cited studies.

claim: Some studies suggested dedifferentiation or loss of Leydig cells after GAHT.
source: Some studies also suggested dedifferentiation of Sertoli cells (Schulze, 1988) and/or dedifferentiation or loss of Leydig cells (Rodriguez-Rigau et al., 1977; Sapino et al., 1987; Schulze, 1988; Venizelos and Paradinas, 1988; Kisman et al., 1990; Matoso et al., 2018; Cornejo et al., 2022).
evidence: This is a summary of findings from multiple cited studies.

claim: Discrepancies in previous findings may stem from limited sample sizes in most studies and differences in GAHT regimens.
source: These discrepancies may stem from the limited sample sizes in most studies and the differences in GAHT regimens, involving diverse hormone types, dosages, modes of administration or adherence to treatment (Hembree et al., 2009).
evidence: This is an interpretation of why previous studies showed variable results, with citation support.

claim: Previous findings on testicular cells mainly relied on histological outcomes and lacked the use of specific markers to accurately identify the condition of these cells.
source: Moreover, previous findings on the testicular cells mainly relied on histological outcomes and lacked the use of specific markers to accurately identify the condition of these cells.
evidence: This is a critique of previous research methodology based on literature review.

claim: Testosterone is essential for maintaining the differentiated phenotype and function of Sertoli cells.
source: As T is essential for maintaining the differentiated phenotype and function of Sertoli cells (Gholami et al., 2023), these findings suggest that the disrupted steroid hormone levels after GAHT could cause a partial dedifferentiation of the Sertoli cells (Nistal et al., 2013).
evidence: This is cited from published literature.

claim: Disrupted steroid hormone levels after GAHT could cause a partial dedifferentiation of the Sertoli cells.
source: As T is essential for maintaining the differentiated phenotype and function of Sertoli cells (Gholami et al., 2023), these findings suggest that the disrupted steroid hormone levels after GAHT could cause a partial dedifferentiation of the Sertoli cells (Nistal et al., 2013).
evidence: This is an interpretation based on the study findings and cited literature.

claim: Estrogens promote Leydig cell engulfment by macrophages by stimulating Leydig cells to produce growth arrest-specific 6.
source: Interestingly, estrogens promote Leydig cell engulfment by macrophages by stimulating Leydig cells to produce growth arrest-specific 6, which mediates phagocytosis of apoptotic cells by bridging cells with surface-exposed phosphatidylserine to macrophage receptors (Yu et al., 2014).
evidence: This mechanism is cited from published literature.

claim: INSL3 is exclusively produced by Leydig cells and is only indirectly regulated by the hypothalamic-pituitary-gonadal axis, making it a reliable marker to assess the Leydig cell population size and Leydig cell maturity.
source: INSL3 was used to further assess the Leydig cells, as it is exclusively produced by Leydig cells and is only indirectly regulated by the hypothalamic-pituitary-gonadal axis, making it a reliable marker to assess the Leydig cell population size and Leydig cell maturity (Ivell et al., 2013; Anand-Ivell et al., 2022).
evidence: This is cited from published literature.

claim: Excessive E2 concentrations might suppress INSL3 expression.
source: Nevertheless, it should be considered that excessive E2 concentrations might suppress INSL3 expression (Laguë and Tremblay, 2009; Sansone et al., 2019).
evidence: This is cited from published literature.

claim: Adequate testosterone levels, produced by Leydig cells, are essential for supporting spermatogenesis.
source: This was expected since adequate T levels, produced by Leydig cells, are essential for supporting spermatogenesis (Smith and Walker, 2014).
evidence: This is cited from published literature.

claim: Leydig cells tend to lose functionality with increasing age.
source: This could again be attributed to variations in GAHT sensitivity related to age but also to the tendency of Leydig cells to lose functionality with increasing age (Anand-Ivell et al., 2022).
evidence: This is cited from published literature.

claim: CYP11a1 only gradually appears in Leydig cells around puberty.
source: However, as shown by Guo and colleagues, and reflected in the prepubertal controls, CYP11a1 only gradually appears in Leydig cells around puberty (Guo et al., 2020), meaning that truly immature Leydig cells could not be identified using this approach.
evidence: This is cited from published literature and confirmed by control tissue observations.

claim: Spermatogonia present in transgender tissue express transcripts of early undifferentiated spermatogonia, similar to the early undifferentiated spermatogonia in cisgender tissue of all ages.
source: In fact, it has been shown that the spermatogonia present in transgender tissue express transcripts of early undifferentiated spermatogonia, similar to the early undifferentiated spermatogonia in cisgender tissue of all ages (Guo et al., 2020).
evidence: This is cited from published literature.

claim: Transgender Sertoli cells exhibit a phenotype similar to that of Sertoli cells in Sertoli cell-only tubule disorders where immaturity markers and AR are concomitantly expressed.
source: Moreover, we show that transgender Sertoli cells exhibit a phenotype similar to that of Sertoli cells in Sertoli cell-only tubule disorders where immaturity markers and AR are concomitantly expressed (Sharpe et al., 2003).
evidence: This comparison is based on the study findings and cited literature.

claim: Leydig and PTMCs in the testes of trans women display altered transcriptomes not related to rejuvenation.
source: Noteworthy, Leydig and PTMCs in the testes of trans women display altered transcriptomes not related to rejuvenation (Guo et al., 2020), which may point to potential malignant alterations due to GAHT and to the important role of T in keeping these cells healthy after maturation.
evidence: This is cited from published literature.

claim: A recent report shows no increased risk of testicular cancer in GAHT patients.
source: Although a recent report shows no increased risk of testicular cancer in GAHT patients (de Nie et al., 2022b), several other reports point to a tight correlation between elevated levels of estrogen and germ or Leydig cell cancers (Huseby, 1980; Bouskine et al., 2008; Chandhoke et al., 2018; Fénichel and Chevalier, 2019).
evidence: This is cited from published literature.

claim: Several reports point to a tight correlation between elevated levels of estrogen and germ or Leydig cell cancers.
source: Although a recent report shows no increased risk of testicular cancer in GAHT patients (de Nie et al., 2022b), several other reports point to a tight correlation between elevated levels of estrogen and germ or Leydig cell cancers (Huseby, 1980; Bouskine et al., 2008; Chandhoke et al., 2018; Fénichel and Chevalier, 2019).
evidence: This is cited from multiple published studies.

claim: Routine pathology examination following orchidectomy was advised even though malignant findings were rare.
source: In another recent report, routine pathology examination following orchidectomy was advised even though malignant findings were rare (Bonapace-Potvin et al., 2022).
evidence: This is cited from published literature.

claim: Alterations at the testis level result from a combination of estrogen and anti-androgen therapy, and not solely from testosterone suppression.
source: Also interesting to note, the GO term 'response to estrogen' (eight genes, adjusted p-value<1.55e-2) is part of P5, showing that alterations at the testis level result from a combination of estrogen and anti-androgen therapy, and not solely from T suppression.
evidence: This is an interpretation based on gene expression analysis findings.

claim: Transgender testicular tissue which expresses AMH, AR, CYP11a1, INSL3, and ACTA2, contains spermatogonia, and exhibits minimal tubular hyalinization, may serve as a valuable alternative for prepubertal and peripubertal testicular tissue in research.
source: Our findings suggest that transgender testicular tissue which expresses AMH, AR, CYP11a1, INSL3, and ACTA2 contains spermatogonia, and exhibits minimal tubular hyalinization, may serve as a valuable alternative for this.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the study findings regarding tissue characteristics.

claim: A recent study showed that testicular cells from GAHT-treated trans women can preserve their function, and that spermatogenesis can be successfully restored.
source: Moreover, a recent study showed that testicular cells from GAHT-treated trans women can preserve their function, and that spermatogenesis can be successfully restored (de Nie et al., 2023).
evidence: This is cited from published literature.

claim: The use of digested trans women's testicular tissue for the testing of compounds in vitro has been described in the literature.
source: In fact, the use of digested trans women's testicular tissue for the testing of compounds in vitro has been described in the literature (Mincheva et al., 2020).
evidence: This is cited from published literature.

claim: Hormone levels were measured during the last visit before SRS rather than on the day of surgery, explaining suboptimal E2 serum levels in many participants.
source: The first limitation is that the hormone levels were measured during the last visit before SRS rather than on the day of surgery, and not considering the time of last administration and blood draw, explaining suboptimal E2 serum levels in many participants.
evidence: This is acknowledged as a study limitation.

claim: Certain transgender-specific factors such as tucking, wearing tight underwear, and having a low masturbation frequency might have negatively impacted testicular health.
source: It is possible that certain transgender-specific factors such as tucking, wearing tight underwear, and having a low masturbation frequency might have negatively impacted their testicular health (de Nie et al., 2020).
evidence: This is cited as a potential confounding factor from published literature.

claim: All trans women in this study showed normal serum testosterone values before initiating GAHT.
source: Nevertheless, all trans women in this study showed normal serum T values before initiating GAHT.
evidence: This is stated as a fact about the study cohort.

claim: The practice in ENIGI has changed over recent years toward reduction in prescribed daily CPA dosage or abandoning CPA altogether in favor of GnRH analogues as anti-androgen treatment.
source: Since in ENIGI the practice has changed over the recent years toward reduction in prescribed daily CPA dosage (Kuijpers et al., 2021) or abandoning CPA altogether in favor of GnRH analogues as anti-androgen treatment, a re-evaluation in this more recent cohort is advisable.
evidence: This is stated as a change in clinical practice with citation support.

claim: Trans women undergoing GAHT with E2 and CPA exhibit a partially rejuvenated spermatogonial stem cell niche.
source: In summary, our findings show that trans women undergoing GAHT with E2 and CPA exhibit a partially rejuvenated spermatogonial stem cell niche.
evidence: This is the main conclusion summarizing the study findings.

claim: In the tubular wall of trans women, PTMCs continue to express ACTA2 although in a disturbed pattern, likely due to fibrotic processes.
source: In the tubular wall, PTMCs continue to express ACTA2 although in a disturbed pattern, likely due to fibrotic processes.
evidence: This is a summary conclusion based on the ACTA2 staining results.

claim: There is evidence of a regressed seminiferous epithelium and a collapsing lumen in trans women.
source: Additionally, there is evidence of a regressed seminiferous epithelium and a collapsing lumen.
evidence: This is a summary conclusion based on histological findings.

claim: Sertoli cells in trans women have partially dedifferentiated (expression of both AMH and AR) and resemble those of peripubertal boys.
source: Sertoli cells have partially dedifferentiated (expression of both AMH and AR) and resemble those of peripubertal boys.
evidence: This is a summary conclusion based on immunofluorescence findings.

claim: Leydig cells in trans women show a distribution similar to that of peripubertal tissue and a decreased INSL3 expression.
source: Leydig cells also show a distribution similar to that of peripubertal tissue and a decreased INSL3 expression.
evidence: This is a summary conclusion based on immunofluorescence findings.

claim: The transcriptomic profiles of transgender and control testicular tissue reveal ongoing inflammation.
source: The transcriptomic profiles of transgender and control testicular tissue reveal ongoing inflammation but also confirm the microscopy findings that point to a loss of mature characteristics - a partial rejuvenation - of the spermatogonial stem cell niche in transgender testicular tissue.
evidence: This is a summary conclusion based on gene expression analysis.

claim: Testicular tissue from trans women holds the potential to be used as a surrogate for (pre)pubertal tissue in in vitro applications.
source: Hence, testicular tissue from trans women holds the potential to be used as a surrogate for (pre)pubertal tissue in in vitro applications.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the overall findings of the study.

claim: The study population consists of 106 trans women exclusively selected from the UZ Gent.
source: The current study population consists of the one (n=97) used in our previous publication (Vereecke et al., 2020), plus nine other participants, totaling n=106 trans women exclusively selected from the UZ Gent.
evidence: This describes the study cohort composition.

claim: The included trans women were at least 16 years of age before starting GAHT.
source: The included trans women underwent a standardized diagnostic procedure and were at least 16 years of age before starting GAHT (Dekker et al., 2016).
evidence: This describes an inclusion criterion for the study.

claim: Treatment protocols were in accordance with the World Professional Association for Transgender Health Standards of Care, Version 7 (WPATH SOC 7).
source: Treatment protocols were in accordance with the World Professional Association for Transgender Health Standards of Care, Version 7 (WPATH SOC 7) (Coleman et al., 2022), and consisted of an oral administration of 2 mg of E2 valerate (ProgynovaVR, Bayer, Diegem, Belgium) twice daily, along with 50 mg of the anti-androgen CPA (AndrocurVR, Bayer, Diegem, Belgium) once daily.
evidence: This describes the treatment protocol used in the study.

claim: For participants aged 45 and above and participants with a previous history of venous thromboembolism, the estrogen treatment consisted of transdermal E2 at a daily dosage of 50–100 mg.
source: For participants aged 45 and above and participants with a previous history of venous thromboembolism, the estrogen treatment consisted of transdermal E2 (DermestrilVR, Besins, Brussels, Belgium) at a daily dosage of 50–100 mg.
evidence: This describes a treatment modification for specific participants.

claim: Hormone therapy was stopped 2 weeks before SRS to reduce the risk of peri-operative thromboembolism.
source: To reduce the risk of peri-operative thromboembolism, hormone therapy was stopped 2 weeks before SRS.
evidence: This describes a clinical protocol used in the study.

claim: Significant correlations were found between serum AMH and the percentage of AMH+ tubules, tissue hyalinization, and progression of spermatogenesis.
source: Significant correlations were found for 'serum AMH' and the 'percentage of AMH+ tubules' (r=0.330), 'tissue hyalinization' (r=−0.289), and 'progression of spermatogenesis' (r=−0.278).
evidence: This is based on correlation analysis of the data.

claim: There were significant differences in Leydig cell functional maturity between the 'No spermatogonia' and 'Partial differentiation' groups.
source: Significant differences could be observed between the 'No spermatogonia' and 'Partial differentiation' groups (p=0.006) and between the 'Only spermatogonia' and 'Partial differentiation' groups (p=0.019).
evidence: This is based on statistical analysis comparing groups.

claim: There were significant differences in Leydig cell functional maturity between the 'Only spermatogonia' and 'Partial differentiation' groups.
source: Significant differences could be observed between the 'No spermatogonia' and 'Partial differentiation' groups (p=0.006) and between the 'Only spermatogonia' and 'Partial differentiation' groups (p=0.019).
evidence: This is based on statistical analysis comparing groups.

claim: No significant differences in Leydig cell functional maturity were observed between the 'No spermatogonia' and 'Only spermatogonia' groups.
source: No significant differences were observed between the 'No spermatogonia' and 'Only spermatogonia' groups (p=0.173).
evidence: This is based on statistical analysis comparing groups.

claim: There are relatively more functionally mature Leydig cells in the 'Partial differentiation' group than in the 'No/Only spermatogonia' groups.
source: It was noted that the score in the 'Partial differentiation' group was higher compared to the 'No/Only spermatogonia' groups, suggesting that there are relatively more functionally mature Leydig cells in the 'Partial differentiation' than in the 'No/Only spermatogonia' groups.
evidence: This is an interpretation based on statistical analysis results.

claim: ACTA2 expression is stimulated by androgens.
source: Apart from this, ACTA2 expression is stimulated by androgens (Schlatt et al., 1993) which are suppressed in trans women undergoing GAHT.
evidence: This is cited from published literature.

claim: Adult Klinefelter syndrome participants typically possess low testosterone levels and exhibit an 'interrupted' or 'absent' ACTA2 pattern.
source: Adult Klinefelter syndrome participants, for example, also typically possess low T levels and exhibit an 'interrupted' or 'absent' ACTA2 pattern (Van Saen et al., 2020).
evidence: This is cited from published literature as a comparison.

claim: PTMCs provide structural support to the seminiferous tubules, contribute to their contractile function, and exhibit a smooth muscle phenotype characterized by intensive expression of ACTA2.
source: The PTMCs provide structural support to the seminiferous tubules, contribute to their contractile function, and exhibit a smooth muscle phenotype characterized by intensive expression of ACTA2, distinguishing them from fibroblasts (Volkmann et al., 2011; Mayerhofer, 2013).
evidence: This is cited from published literature.

claim: Smooth muscle cells are known to shift phenotype in response to changes in the local environment.
source: This may result in a loss of ACTA2 expression, causing a shift in the PTMC phenotype as smooth muscle cells are known to do so in response to changes in the local environment (Owens et al., 2004).
evidence: This is cited from published literature.
